cryo.lose_20K_shield_keep_3K: the 3 K stage would have to lift the full 2.4 kW at 1500 W/W (3.5 MW): it cannot; He-3 warms as in a total loss
cryo.n_plus_1: Cryocooler trains as N+1 units split over buses A and B; the 3 K He-3 stage is the critical one (1.2 t/day if it alone fails, 24 t/day after the sealed hold if everything fails).
cryo.recovery: Re-cooling after a hold: a warmed vessel must be brought back below its relief point; with the 20 K shield back, the 3 K stage recovers ~0.1 K a day per 100 W of spare lift (slow): spare lift capacity sets recovery.

anchors.SP-100: SP-100 GES (1980s-1990s): 100 kWe, ~2.4 MWt, thermoelectric, ~4.6 t total incl. radiator and an unmanned 25 m shadow shield; 7-10 yr life. Scope: whole power system, unmanned dose limits. Used for reactor-core scaling only.
anchors.JIMO: JIMO/Prometheus (2005): 100 kWe Brayton, ~500 kWt, 170 m2 radiator for ~360 kWt; reactor module ~ a few t. Scope: unmanned.
anchors.INL2002: INL multi-MWe space Brayton study: ~3.5 kg/kWe system goal (3-5), called substantial development. Scope: optimistic total incl. radiator, unmanned shield. Not demonstrated.
anchors.Mason2023: Mason, NASA GRC Brayton conversion: MW-class closed Brayton turbo-alternator-compressor + recuperator + gas cooler ~2-5 kg/kWe (conversion only). Brayton component technology flown in none; terrestrial and lab heritage (BRU, 2 kWe-class).
anchors.Kilopower: KRUSTY 2018: 1 kWe-class Stirling, demonstrated on the ground; Fission Surface Power 40 kWe under 6 t (incl. shield for surface use). Scope: whole plant.
anchors.MMRTG: MMRTG: 110 We BOL, 45 kg, ~4.8 kg Pu-238 dioxide, -4.8 %/yr output incl. thermocouple degradation (flight).
anchors.ASRG: Advanced Stirling RG (cancelled 2013): ~130 We, ~32 kg, 4x less Pu-238 than an MMRTG (lab-tested).
anchors.Fusion: No fusion plant has produced net electricity. Compact D-He3 power plant masses in studies span tens of t to hundreds of t; minimum machine size is the dominant unknown. SPECULATIVE within the IGNITION technology frame.
anchors.Decay: Way-Wigner decay heat P/P0 = 0.0622 (t^-0.2 - (t+T)^-0.2), t and T in s (order of magnitude, +/-30 %).

dust.note: Vertex research-mission profile (467 d), not the six-year canon mission: an order-of-magnitude context only.
dust.warning: At 0.016 c a grain covers 4,800 km/s: warning times are milliseconds to seconds; neutral dust ignores fields.

architectures.name: A: 2 x 100 %
architectures.note: Each plant carries the whole design load alone.

architectures.name: B: 2 x 60 %, essentials on either
architectures.note: Either plant alone carries everything that must keep running (crew, cryo, nav, comms, proactive defense).

architectures.name: C: 3+1 modular (N+1)
architectures.note: Four identical modules; any three carry the design load.

architectures.name: C2: 5+1 modular
architectures.note: Smaller modules: more shield discs and controls, better availability.

architectures.name: D: 3+1 modular + dedicated defense buffer
architectures.note: Modules sized for design plus 2 MW to recharge a defense buffer; engagements up to the buffer limit draw the active band from storage (buffer mass listed apart).

architectures.name: E: 2 x 60 % auxiliary fusion (SPECULATIVE)
architectures.note: D-He3 in the IGNITION frame; no fusion plant has made net electricity.

architectures.name: A-bound: 2 x 100 % for continuous active defense
architectures.note: Bounding: the normal active band all cruise.

operating_modes.mode: All units at partial load (hot, sharing)
operating_modes.penalty: every unit accumulates turbomachinery hours and fuel burn; no dormant failures
operating_modes.benefit: a trip loses only its share

operating_modes.mode: Warm standby (reactor at low power, loop hot, TAC idling or stopped)
operating_modes.penalty: decay and idle heat still rejected; standby reactor still needs shielding
operating_modes.benefit: spare unit ready after a trip

operating_modes.mode: Cold standby (subcritical, loop frozen or drained)
operating_modes.start: hours to a day (thaw a Li loop: Li freezes at 454 K; NaK does not)

L1.note: Conversion from the drive hot loop at ~1800 K (Brayton/MHD/direct conversion OPEN); 0.7-3.5 kg/kWe (INL2002 total as the conservative end). The hot-loop pumps (OPEN, 10-100 MW planning) dominate the uncertainty.

radiation.RPS: Pu-238 alpha source: gamma and spontaneous-fission neutrons are weak; ~0.1-1 mSv/h at 1 m unshielded for a kWt-class unit; a few cm of shielding or a few metres of distance suffice beside a refuge.
radiation.fission: A 10-40 kWe fission-Stirling (40-150 kWt) next to the refuge needs a shadow shield of ~1-3 t and tens of metres, or the refuge itself as shield: placing it beside the refuge is not acceptable without it; 20-40 m away on the forward collar is.
radiation.recommendation: Local batteries/fuel cells per ring and refuge for crew-only (no single point), plus one isolated kWe-class RPS or fission-Stirling for mission preservation; cryo at 0.4 MW is beyond any isolated survival source short of L2.

transitions.coast_to_burn: Warm channels drained and purged before the blades heat: L2 loses its coast sink. L2 steps down to hot standby and L1 takes the ship load; L2 decay heat goes to the WARM section margin.

warm_section_in_burn.note: The WARM section rejects its 5 MW in every mode; plant decay heat (~0.05-0.1 MW after an hour) must fit beside the machinery base load or be heat-pumped (6 W of L1 work per W).

transitions.burn_to_coast: Blades cool radiatively from 1800 K to below ~500 K in minutes (thin C/C sheets); hot-loop decay heat sets hours. Channels refill and L2 restarts from hot standby; battery bridges minutes only.
transitions.drive_trip_in_burn: L1 lost with hot blades and drained channels: heat pumps stop, so the WARM section (5 MW) is free for L2 at reduced power (~1.0-1.3 MWe at 25 % efficiency) until the channels refill: crew, cryo, nav keep running; proactive defense (2.5 MW) cannot.
transitions.generator_trip: One unit lost: architecture-dependent (see reliability); the blade channels of the lost unit stay available.
transitions.heat_pump_trip: In a burn: warm heat beyond the WARM section has no sink; defense heat goes to Heat Debt (buffer OPEN) or the active band is shed to proactive within the buffer time.
transitions.radiator_circuit_loss: Plants on separate blades (A on blade 1, B on blade 2) keep independent rejection paths; one shared manifold would be a common mode that defeats plant redundancy.
transitions.emergency_rejection: LOW and WARM sections (1 + 5 MW) are the only surfaces that work in every mode; with blades hot and channels drained they are the ship's whole emergency sink.
